 This post is full-time (35 hours per week), and has funding available until 30 th September 2029 in the first instance. 

 Applications are invited for the position of Research Fellow in Applied AI for the Energy Transition within the James Watt School of Engineering.

 This position offers a unique opportunity to contribute to a major new UKRI-funded Fellowship at the intersection of artificial intelligence, scientific machine learning and subsurface engineering. The research focuses on developing physics-informed machine learning approaches to improve understanding of the subsurface, a critical challenge in the deployment of offshore wind and other net-zero energy infrastructure.

 Prior domain experience in geotechnics, geophysics or offshore engineering is not required. We welcome applications from candidates in machine learning, artificial intelligence, computer science, statistics, data science, engineering, applied mathematics, physics or a closely related discipline.

 The successful candidate will undertake research in physics-informed machine learning, uncertainty quantification, predictive modelling and geospatial data integration to improve subsurface characterisation and support decision-making for offshore renewable energy developments. The research will create opportunities for methodological advances in machine learning and uncertainty-aware modelling while addressing important challenges in offshore renewable energy and the net-zero transition.

 The postholder will join an interdisciplinary team of engineers, data scientists and geophysicists led by Dr Róisín Buckley as part of a UKRI-funded Fellowship. The role offers opportunities to collaborate with leading academic and industrial partners, including researchers across the UK's AI ecosystem in data science and artificial intelligence. In addition, the postholder will have access to world-class experimental and computational facilities and will play a key role in shaping an ambitious research programme at the interface of geophysics, engineering and AI.

 For an informal discussion about the post and research programme, please contact Dr Roisin Buckley on Roisin.Buckley@glasgow.ac.uk 

 All applicants must have the right to live and work in the UK or be eligible to obtain permission to work in the UK.

 This role may be eligible for sponsorship under the Skilled Worker visa route, subject to meeting the relevant Home Office requirements, including any applicable tradeable points criteria. Further information can be found on the University of Glasgow’s UKVI Website . 

 For research and academic roles, we will also consider whether the Global Talent visa route may be available, subject to individual eligibility.

 For more information and to apply please click the 'Apply' button above. 

 Closing date: 29 th November 2026 at 23:45pm 

 We strongly endorse the principles of Athena SWAN, including a supportive and flexible working environment, with commitment from all levels of the organisation in promoting gender equality.

 The School of Computer Science and Electronics Engineering (CSEE) has a long-standing tradition on computer networks and artificial intelligence. In the recent Research Excellence Framework 2021 (REF’2021), CSEE ranked 6th in the UK for research power and 9th for research impact (Grade Point Average).

 The Institute for Analytics and Data Science (IADS) was created in July 2014 to bring together all the University’s expertise and work in analytics and data science. IADS research utilises new forms of data and advanced analytic techniques to tackle social challenges, engage with business and the wider non-academic community, is international in outlook and scope, and multidisciplinary and interdisciplinary by nature.

 Duties of the Role
 The successful candidate will contribute to the EU Horizon-funded SAFARI project, focusing on AI-driven risk assessment and resilience of critical infrastructures.

 Key responsibilities include:

 Conducting research on cyber risk analysis, critical infrastructure resilience, and AI-enabled decision support.

 Developing AI and machine learning methods for anomaly detection, risk prediction, and cascading failure forecasting.

 Designing risk identification and propagation models for cyber incidents, system failures, and environmental disruptions.

 Investigating continuous resilience improvement through predictive modelling, learning-based feedback loops, and digital twin simulations.

 Collaborating with international project partners, contributing to project deliverables, publishing research findings, and supporting future research proposals.

 A full list of duties and responsibilities of the role can be found within the job pack. 

 Skills/Qualifications
 Essential:

 A PhD (or near completion) in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Artificial Intelligence, Computer Networks, or a closely related discipline.

 Research experience in network resilience, risk analysis, or cyber resilience of critical infrastructures or distributed systems.

 Knowledge of AI, machine learning, and optimisation techniques.

 Programming skills in C/C++ and Python.

 Evidence of high-quality research activity and a developing publication record.

 Strong communication and collaborative research skills.

 A full list of essential and desirable criteria can be found within the job pack. 

 This is a research position, and no teaching duties are associated to this post. This is a fixed-term position for a maximum of 25 months.

 LSE is committed to building a diverse, equitable and truly inclusive university 

 Salary from £37,244 to £42,397 per annum inclusive with potential to progress to £45,358 pa inclusive of London allowance 

 Funding is available to support this position until 31 December 2027. 

 The TPI Centre is an independent, authoritative source of research and data on the progress of corporate and sovereign entities in transitioning to a low-carbon economy. It is the academic partner of the Transition Pathway Initiative (TPI), a global initiative led by asset owners and supported by asset managers, aimed at helping investors and other stakeholders assess company, bank and sovereign progress on the transition to a low-carbon economy and supporting efforts to address climate change. 

 We are hiring four roles : one will primarily be based in the Management Quality team; three will primarily be based in the Net Zero Strategies team. 

 Please state if you have a preference as part of your application. 

 You may also be asked to support other projects as required. 

 Management Quality evaluates the quality of companies’ management of their greenhouse gas emissions and of risks and opportunities related to the low-carbon transition. 

 Net Zero Strategies assesses companies’ transition plans across their business segments to evaluate how they plan to reach their decarbonisation targets. 

 The role is to provide high-quality analysis by: 

 Conducting in-depth data analysis of company disclosures, identifying appropriate methods of investigation or analysis based on the available data and assessment objectives. 

 Collecting , processing and performing quality checks on corporate data that feed into the TPI Centre’s Management Quality/Net Zero Strategies assessment frameworks. 

 Conveying complex conceptual ideas and information which are highly detailed, technical or specialist.

 Interpreting and analysing patterns or trends in data.

 Managing large-scale databases.

 Candidates should have: 

 Good understanding of issues in sustainable finance and investment with relevant professional experience in climate change and/or sustainable finance.  

 Strong analytical and quantitative skills in Excel and spreadsheet-based modelling, as well as knowledge of basic statistical methods for data analysis and interpretation. 

 Exposure to managing large databases and proficient IT skills for visualising and presenting data and developing high-quality reports, presentations and other outputs.

 We offer the opportunity to work with a world-leading research centre, in a vibrant and inclusive team culture, with an occupational pension scheme, hybrid working, generous annual leave and excellent training and development opportunities. 

 For further information about the post, please see the how to apply document , job description  and the person specification . 

 To apply for this post, please click the 'Apply' button above . If you have any technical queries with applying on the online system, please use the “contact us” links at the bottom of the LSE Jobs page. Should you have any queries about the role, please email gri.hr@lse.ac.uk 

 The closing date for receipt of applications is 13 November 2026 (23.59 UK time). Regrettably, we are unable to accept any late applications. 

 Shortlisted candidates will be required to complete a task. Interviews are anticipated to be held in November/December 2026. 

 If you delete or withdraw your application, you will not be able to re-apply for this vacancy. Feedback will only be provided upon request if you attend an interview.

About the role

We are seeking a Research Associate to join our team as part of the AI for Chemistry (AIchemy) hub, specialising in multi-modal generative AI for small molecules conditioned on experimental spectra. 

AIchemy, funded by the EPSRC, is a research hub dedicated to advancing artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) in the field of chemistry. AIchemy aims to develop new AI approaches and promote their adoption within the chemistry community. The hub unites AI researchers from various subdisciplines, including computer science and both experimental and computational chemists, fostering connectivity, training, networking, and state-of-the-art research.

This position offers an exciting opportunity to design and implement novel algorithms in generative AI applicable across large-scale multi-modal chemistry data (including experimental properties) while collaborating with the larger team at Imperial College London and across the UK-wide AIchemy Hub to collectively advance AI in chemistry.

The Research Associate will co-develop the project in partnership with experimental and theoretical chemists, and machine-learning academics across the Chemistry and Computing Departments. This position provides academic freedom and will leverage the deep scientific base of the broader AIchemy Hub, including self-driving labs and high-throughput synthesis and analysis setups, enabling you to make a significant contribution to the field. You will join a cohort of computational and experimental researchers, technicians, and software engineers working at the AI/Chemistry interface and a thriving community of events and initiatives that you can take a role in shaping.

What you would be doing

Implement and develop methods for the computational generation of small molecules and materials, which have the potential to be synthesised by experimental collaborators.
Explore how multi-modal chemistry data (molecular and crystal structures, experimental spectra, computed and measured properties) can be incorporated into the generation process.
Collaborate and cooperate with partners of AIchemy and other AI for Science projects funded by the UK EPSRC.
Act as the representative for Imperial College London in meetings, conference calls and present research at conferences, workshops, and open days, and publish research results in journals.
Assist in the supervision of undergraduate and postgraduate research students and research assistants as required, designing projects and helping make decisions about research directions.
Take the initiative in the planning of research, co-developing your project with a range of academic mentors.
Develop and maintain open-source software together with other group members.

What we are looking for

Practical experience of developing and applying generative model architectures, such as diffusion, flow-matching or autoregressive models, to molecules or materials.
Knowledge of machine learning representations for molecules and materials, such as graph neural networks and equivariant networks.
Machine learning algorithms and model development experience.
Successful experience of working with multidisciplinary experimental and theory collaborators.
Practical experience within a research environment and publications in relevant peer-reviewed journals.

What we can offer you

The chance to join the AIchemy Hub, a multidisciplinary team working at the forefront of AI in Chemistry.
The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity.
Grow your career: gain access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression.
As a member of research staff you have 10 development days to use to develop your skills and explore your career prospects
Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days off a year and generous pension schemes).
Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing.

 Salary (£): Research Grade 7: £40,178 - £48,700 per annum A less experienced candidate may be appointed at Grade 6 (£36, 360 – £42,434 per annum), with a commensurate adjustment in either the essential criteria, responsibilities or duties. 

 We are looking for an outstanding researcher for a joint project between the University of Oxford and an industrial partner, Great Sky. The postholder will develop an implementation of a model of information processing in the brain, called predictive coding, in hardware employing superconducting computational circuits. The research will employ mathematical analysis and computer simulations to investigate how the predictive coding model can be adjusted so it can be implemented in the neuromorphic hardware, while preserving the computational advantages of the model. 

 Predictive coding is a brain-inspired model which learns with fewer examples than traditional artificial neural networks, used in artificial intelligence (AI). Therefore, it has a potential to speed up training of AI models. However, simulating this model on current digital computers is slow, as they are not optimized for the computations which predictive coding requires. By contrast, the new hardware developed by Great Sky performs computations in a fundamentally different way, which is compatible with the requirements of the predictive coding model. Implementing predictive coding on this hardware will unlock the advantages of predictive coding, resulting in faster and more energy-efficient training of AI.

 The postholder will be co-supervised by Rafal Bogacz from University of Oxford and Jeff Shainline from Great Sky. The post holder will work as a part of an interdisciplinary team including computational neuroscientists studying learning in brain networks in Oxford and will collaborate with engineers developing neuromorphic hardware at Great Sky. The post holder will also be a member of a research group of Professor Rafal Bogacz, and based in the Brain Network Dynamics Unit, which includes an interdisciplinary community of neurobiologists, engineers and computational scientists.

Research Assistant/Research Associate (Qualitative Research)
Requisition ID:  29790
Location:  

Newcastle, GB

Contract Type:  Fixed Term
Working Pattern:  Full Time
Posted Date:  30 Oct 2026

 

Salary: 

Research Assistant:  £34,630 -  £36,320 per annum

Research Associate: £37,369 -  £41,885 per annum

 

Newcastle University is a great place to work, with excellent benefits. We have a generous holiday package; plus the opportunity to buy more, great pension schemes and a number of health and wellbeing initiatives to support you.

 

Closing Date: 01 December 2026

 

The role

 

We are seeking to appoint a Research Assistant/Associate (RA) with a specialism in qualitative research methods to work on an interdisciplinary project entitled, The Night Shift 1850-present: Reimagining Sleep, Work and Wellbeing for Healthcare Professionals in English and Scottish Hospitals, led by PI Dr Kristin Hussey and funded by the Wellcome Trust. The project is hosted in the School of History, Classics & Archaeology, which has a vibrant and active research culture: https://www.ncl.ac.uk/hca/about/

 

The Night Shift is an ambitious project which aims to radically re-imagine sleep work and wellbeing for healthcare professionals working at night in England and Scotland. The project examines how longstanding workplace cultures and professional identities have normalised unsafe and unsustainable working conditions. Working with healthcare professionals at NHS Trusts, the postholder will use qualitative methods—including interviews, focus groups and witness seminars—to explore how staff experience and manage night work. The role will contribute to developing interventions to improve staff wellbeing.

 

This is an excellent opportunity for an early career researcher to develop experience in interdisciplinary research, scholarly editing, project management, impact and public engagement, and sole-authored publications. The RA will be provided with academic and pastoral support within the School, and training will be provided to develop their competencies. Newcastle University is a signatory to the Concordat to support researchers’ career development which entitles researchers up to 10 days annually of personal CPD activities. 

 

This post is a (maximum) 60-month fixed term Research Assistant/Associate in History, and a full-time appointment. The successful candidate will start work as soon as possible after 1 March 2027, ending no later than April 18, 2032. Flexible working is welcome, but the postholder must be willing to travel for fieldwork and other research/engagement activities.

 

Applicants with minority and/or host community backgrounds are particularly encouraged to apply. Should the successful applicant require a UK Visa for this role, they will be eligible to apply under the Endorsed Funder Route of the Global Talent Visa. The University will support the applicant through this process.

 

As part of our commitment to career development for research colleagues, the University has developed 3 levels of Research Innovation Role Profiles.pdf.  These profiles set out firstly the generic competencies and responsibilities expected of role holders at each level and, secondly, the general qualifications and experiences needed for entry at a particular level.

 

Newcastle University is committed to the responsible use of research metrics as part of our research culture and research strategy. We advocate for the transparent, appropriate, and inclusive use of metrics, guided by expert judgment, to support high-quality, impactful research that is open, collaborative and sustainable. Click here for our full policy statement on the Responsible use of Research Metrics. 

 

Contact for the post is Dr Kristin Hussey: kristin.hussey@newcastle.ac.uk 

 

To apply, please upload an up-to-date CV and cover letter outlining how you meet the essential job criteria. Please also upload one writing sample (e.g. journal article, book chapter, or thesis chapter) that you feel best reflects your research (10,000 words max). 

 

 

Key Accountabilities

 

•    Work closely with the project PI and others in the team to carry out research relating to The Night Shift 1850-present: Reimagining Sleep, Work and Wellbeing for Healthcare Professionals in English and Scottish Hospitals
•    Work closely with the PI and NHS Research and Development Teams to develop recruitment materials and obtain ethical permissions for semi-structured interviews and focus groups with healthcare professionals and nursing students
•    Conduct interviews and focus groups with night workers at North East NHS Trusts (in person and online), and analyse the data collected
•    Undertake two periods of knowledge exchange at the National Center for the Working Enviornment (NFA) in Copenhagen, Denmark
•    Collaborate with the project team and partners to deliver public and policy outputs including an exhibition, training materials and a policy toolkit

 

 

Research Assistant

•    Collect, analyse and interpret research data and draw conclusions on the outcomes
•    Co-ordinate own work with that of others, use problem solving to affect the achievement of research objectives and contribute to the planning of the project(s)
•    Present information on research progress and outcomes to a Principal Investigator or groups overseeing the research project
•    Write up results from own research activity and provide input into the research project’s dissemination, in whatever form (report, papers, chapters, books)
•    Use research resources (including, where required, laboratories, workshops and specialist equipment) as appropriate

 

Research Associate

•    Contribute ideas, including enhancements to the technical or methodological aspects of the project
•    Determine appropriate methodologies for research
•    Assess research findings for the need/scope for further investigations
•    Contribute to the writing up of the research and its dissemination, either through seminar and conference presentations or through publications
•    Present research findings, either at conferences or through publications in reputable outlets appropriate to the discipline
•    Contribute to grant applications submitted by others and develop own research objectives and proposals for funding

 

The Person (Essential)

 

Knowledge, Skills and Experience 

 

Research Assistant

•    Experience of recruiting, conducting, transcribing and analysing interviews with participants
•    Experience of carrying out research in healthcare settings andfamiliarity with ethical approvals processes 
•    Experience of developing and organsing and/or contributing towards the organisation of public engagement events 
•    Outstanding communication skills for realising research aims, public engagement and outreach, as well as those necessary to work successfully as part of a team
•    Attention to detail and ability to work at high levels of accuracy 
•    Ability to present complex information effectively to a range of audiences
•    Proven ability to analyse data and write-up results
•    Experience of working collaboratively with colleagues
•    Excellent IT skills in all major office applications and with experience with  NVivo software desirable
•    The ability to use personal initiative and creativity to solve research problems

 

In addition for Research Associate

•    Awareness of the research environment
•    High level of analytical and problem-solving capacity
•    Ability to communicate complex information with clarity 
•    Experience of presentations at conferences and/or in high-quality publications

 

Attributes and Behaviour

•    Commitment to working positively as a member of a multi-skilled research team 
•    Ability to negotiate and prioritise multiple, competing responsibilities and to work to deadlines
•      Willingness to work flexibly, responsively and sensitively to the needs of project participants
•    Commitment to continued professional development
•    Understanding of good practice in equality, inclusion and diversity

 

Qualifications

Research Assistant

•    Masters Degree in Sociology, Geography, Medical Humanities, History or another relevant subject or discpline or PhD in progress

 

In addition for Research Associate

•    Awarded PhD in Sociology, Geography, Medical Humanities, History or another relevant subject or discpline

 

 

Newcastle University is a global University where everyone is treated with dignity and respect.  As a University of Sanctuary, we aim to provide a welcoming place of safety for all, offering opportunities to people fleeing violence and persecution.

 

We are committed to being a fully inclusive university which actively recruits, supports and retains colleagues from all sectors of society.  We value diversity as well as celebrate, support and thrive on the contributions of all of our employees and the communities they represent.  We are proud to be an equal opportunities employer and encourage applications from individuals who can complement our existing teams, we believe that success is built on having teams whose backgrounds and experiences reflect the diversity of our university and student population.

 

At Newcastle University we hold a Gold Athena Swan award in recognition of our good employment practices for the advancement of gender equality.  We also hold a Race Equality Charter Bronze award in recognition of our work towards tackling race inequality in higher education REC.  We are a Disability Confident employer and will offer an interview to disabled applicants who meet the essential criteria for the role as part of the offer and interview scheme.

 

In addition, we are a member of the Euraxess initiative supporting researchers in Europe.

 The Department of Psychiatry is based on the Warneford Hospital site in Oxford – a friendly, welcoming place of work with an international reputation for excellence. The Department has a substantial research programme, with major funding from Medical Research Council (MRC), Wellcome Trust and National Institute for Health Research (NIHR) and provides highly rated medical training in psychiatry. The Head of Department is Professor Belinda Lennox.

 We are looking for a Senior Postdoctoral Researcher to join MARGINS (Mental health And Restrictions: Generating new INSights) in the Department of Psychiatry.   

 About the Role 

 The post is full-time and funded for two years. It is based in the Department of Psychiatry at the Warneford Hospital. Applicants must be available to start by 1 February 2027 at the latest. 

 The postholder will normally be expected to work on site for a minimum of three days per week, reflecting the importance of close collaboration with the wider MARGINS research team. The remaining working time may be undertaken flexibly/hybrid, subject to agreement with the line manager and the operational requirements of the project.   

 MARGINS is part of a research programme investigating the impact of proposed policy changes to online technology on children and young people. This comprises three complementary research streams and you will work across all three, providing senior quantitative and methodological leadership across the programme. 

 Working closely with Professor Mina Fazel, Dr Holly Bear, Dr Emma Soneson, the project's statistical lead and international collaborators, you will lead the development of research questions and analytical approaches within the agreed aims of MARGINS, generating original ideas and identifying opportunities for further analyses.

 In addition, you will lead and develop complex quantitative analyses, using large-scale cross-sectional, longitudinal and international datasets and contribute to the interpretation and integration of findings and to high-quality research publications, reports and presentations.

 You will hold a relevant PhD/DPhil in a health, behavioural or social science discipline (for example, psychology, epidemiology, public health or mental health research), with post-qualification research experience.

Part time fixed term

Salary: £49,798 to £61,165 per annum (£19,919 to £24,466 pro rata)

About York St John University

Situated in the heart of the historic city of York, with the addition of our London Campus, York St John University has a long and proud tradition as a distinguished higher education provider.

Our success is founded on the quality of academic teaching and research, our thriving campus environments, our professional and pastoral support, and our values of an inclusive, innovative and ambitious community with a strong sense of belonging.

The Team

You will join the Institute for Health and Care Improvement (IHCI), a vibrant and growing interdisciplinary research environment committed to delivering high-quality, impactful research that improves health and care outcomes.

The Institute works in partnership with local, regional and national organisations across health, care and the voluntary sector, with a strong emphasis on collaboration, co-production and real-world impact.

The Role

We are seeking to appoint a Health Services Research Fellow (14.8 hours per week) to contribute to the development of high-quality, impactful applied health research within the Institute.

The post is offered on a two-year fixed-term basis, with any extension subject to the successful securing of additional external funding.

We are looking for an ambitious researcher with a strong and developing track record in applied health research, alongside substantial previous professional experience working as an allied health professional, nurse or midwife.

The successful candidate will have a PhD or professional doctorate and be able to demonstrate a track record of research activity, with clear potential to develop their research leadership, secure external funding and deliver meaningful impact on health and care.

You will have dedicated time to advance your own programme of applied health research, building on your professional expertise and existing research achievements. Working collaboratively with colleagues and external partners, you will contribute to the development and delivery of research projects, funding applications, publications and activities that support improvements in health and care.

As part of the application process, applicants will be asked to submit a brief research proposal (maximum two pages) outlining:

Their proposed programme of applied health research during the fellowship, including anticipated activities and outputs.
How the proposed research builds on their existing expertise and achievements, and contributes to their longer-term research ambitions.
Opportunities to develop collaborations, generate impact and secure external research funding.

Proposals should demonstrate a clear and feasible programme of work appropriate to the duration and part-time nature of the fellowship.

Key Responsibilities

Conduct high-quality, impactful applied health research.
Develop and lead research projects and collaborations, drawing on clinical expertise and experience.
Prepare and contribute to external research funding applications.
Produce high-quality research outputs, including peer-reviewed publications, reports and conference presentations.
Build productive relationships with health and care organisations, practitioners, patients and other stakeholders.
Contribute to the wider research culture of the Institute, including supporting and mentoring other researchers where appropriate.
Ensure research is conducted in accordance with relevant ethical, governance and regulatory requirements.

About You

You will have:

A PhD or professional doctorate in a relevant health-related discipline.
Substantial previous professional experience working as an allied health professional, nurse or midwife.
A strong and developing track record in applied health research, demonstrated through high-quality research outputs, collaborations and other relevant achievements.
Experience of developing and delivering research projects, with evidence of research leadership or clear potential to progress towards greater independence.
Strong knowledge of relevant research methodologies and their application to real-world health and care challenges.
Experience of contributing to external research funding applications, with the ability to develop competitive proposals and attract research funding.
Experience of supporting the research development of others, including postgraduate researchers or less experienced colleagues.
Excellent communication, organisational and interpersonal skills, and a commitment to collaborative working.

Current or previous registration with the HCPC, NMC or an equivalent professional regulatory body would be advantageous.

We welcome applications from researchers at different stages of their careers who can demonstrate the experience, achievements and potential to make a significant contribution to the Institute's research ambitions.

Additional Information

This fellowship offers an opportunity to advance your research career within a supportive and collaborative academic environment, with dedicated time to develop your research programme, strengthen your publication record and build towards external research funding.

Unfortunately this role is not eligible for Skilled Worker Visa sponsorship however we welcome your application if you are able to evidence right to work in the UK via an alternative route.

It is anticipated that the selection process will include an interview and presentation. Further details will be provided to shortlisted candidates.

For informal enquiries, please contact Professor Garry Tew at g.tew@yorksj.ac.uk.

To learn more about the Institute for Health and Care Improvement, please visit: yorksj.ac.uk/ihci.

We offer a range of family friendly and inclusive policies and facilities and welcome applications from individuals from underrepresented backgrounds. As part of our commitment to providing an inclusive working environment, consideration is given to all requests for job share or flexible working arrangements.

This vacancy is scheduled to close on the date indicated at the bottom of this advert, but we encourage you to please apply as early as possible as we may consider closing earlier if we receive a high level of applications.  If the vacancy is closed earlier, all pending applicants will be notified and provided with 24 hours' notice to submit an application.

Application process support

We are keen to support you throughout the recruitment process.  Before starting your application please refer to the attached candidate application form guidance below which provides advice about completing the application process.

If you require a reasonable adjustment in order to apply for this position please contact vacancies@yorksj.ac.uk.  Within the application form there is an opportunity for you to request a reasonable adjustment at the interview stage of the process, however if you wish to discuss this in further detail at any point  in the process please do not hesitate to contact us. The following resource may help you adapt the device you are using to apply to suit your needs My Computer My Way (abilitynet.org.uk)

Please note that CVs are not accepted in place of the application form.  Within the application process you will be asked to answer a selection of work-related questions. Our aim is to get to know you, and understand your individual skills and experience, and how you would apply these within the role.  We are aware that AI can be helpful in shaping your responses, but we encourage you to share your answers in your own words.

Our benefits package

We offer a wide range of employee benefits including - 

- Excellent annual leave entitlement, including five discretionary university closure days over the Christmas period

- Disability leave (applies to staff who have disclosed a disability and is also available to staff with disabled dependants)

- Pension scheme

- Health Cash Plan after six months service

- Employee Assistance Programme

- Paid leave for Armed Forces Reservists

- On-campus courses, one-to-one tutorials, and online resources to help you develop your digital skills and work with new software

- Relocation expenses package for certain roles

- Reimbursement of Skilled Worker Visa application fees and Visa loan scheme for additional costs (if applicable to the role)

Further information about life at YSJ

Our attached 'further information' document below provides further information about our culture, achievements and testimonials from our employees. 

Read more about our culture, inclusive community, working arrangements and benefits for York St John employees

Read the latest news, views and stories from our staff and students. 

Read more about our commitment to managing and reducing our environmental impact and to promoting sustainable development wherever we can.

Role Description

The Environment and Geography Department brings together researchers with diverse interests in environment and geography. The successful candidate will be part of a supportive and community-oriented department with a strong commitment to upholding our core values (embracing diversity, making a positive difference, environmental sustainability, being friendly and helpful, and always learning). The department is proud to hold an Athena Swan Silver Award.

The Department wishes to recruit a Research Associate with excellent qualitative research skills and experience of conducting independent or collaborative research for a newly funded York-Maastricht Partnership Project on LGBTQ-affirming older adults’ housing. The project will explore the global geography and characteristics of LGBTQ-affirming older adults’ housing, and investigate residents’ lived experiences of this housing. This is an exciting opportunity to work in a small research team that involves researchers from the University of York and Maastricht University to undertake an important literature review and desktop and case study research.

Role

You will work under the supervision of Dr Katherine Brookfield. You will identify and synthesis relevant research in the academic and grey literature on LGBTQ-affirming older adults’ housing. You will undertake desktop research and conduct interviews with relevant housing providers, policymakers and third-sector actors to map the global geography and identify the characteristics of LGBTQ-affirming older adults’ housing schemes. You will complete case study research (e.g. interviews, focus groups, non-participant observation) with the residents and staff of an LGBTQ-affirming older adults’ housing scheme to explore residents’ lived experiences. You will also support Dr Brookfield in the day to day management of the project. The role is anticipated to involve some UK travel for fieldwork.

Skills, Experience & Qualification needed

A PhD in a relevant subject area or equivalent experience.

Sufficient knowledge in a relevant subject, such as the lived experiences of older LGBTQ adults, older adults’ housing experiences, age-friendly housing, to be able to engage in high-quality research.

Knowledge of a range of qualitative research techniques and methodologies

Highly developed communication skills to engage effectively with a wide range of stakeholders and audiences, both orally and in writing, using a range of media.

Ability to work as part of a team and also to work independently using your own initiative.

A collaborative ethos.

Role Description

A brief overview of the role, project and or department

We are looking for an enthusiastic and motivated full-time Postdoctoral Research Associate to join the group of Dr Ioannis Kourtzelis to work on the regulation of innate immune responses. The aim of our research is to identify macrophage - mediated mechanisms shaping health and disease. 

The Hull York Medical School (ranked 10 in the UK), the associated Department of Biology and York Biomedical Research Institute are recognised world leaders in biomedical research. You will join a vibrant environment of scientific researchers who are dedicated to tackling these important problems in global health. We are committed to fostering a supportive environment where staff and students can thrive, contribute their best, and achieve their full potential. We take great pride in holding the Athena Swan Gold Award.

Role

This is an exciting position funded by the Advanced Research and Invention Agency (ARIA). This project is part of the Sustained Viral Resilience programme and includes a collaboration between groups at the Universities of York, Cambridge, Birmingham, University College London, King’s College London and Queen Mary, University of London. This position will be based at York. Anticipated start date for this position is March-April 2027. The end date for the current phase of funding is 31 May 2030.  The aim of this project is to characterise the effects of ‘sustained innate immunoprophylactics’ (SIIPs) that are based on engineered lipid nanoparticlestargeting lung - mediated immune regulation. 

You will be a postdoctoral-level researcher with interests in the macrophage - mediated mechanisms of immune regulation. Specifically, the post-holder will be expected to lead the project in relation to animal studies and interact with other partners within an ARIA-funded consortium. 

Skills, Experience & Qualification needed
The successful candidates will have a PhD in a biomedical sciences discipline with a focus on immunology 
Knowledge in a range of research techniques and methodologies including in depth expertise in mouse models, cellular immunology (flow cytometry, fluorescence microscopy) to engage in high quality research  
Strong understanding of current concepts in immunology 
The successful candidate must have experience of carrying out both independent and collaborative research, writing up research work for publication and a willingness to contribute to the process of securing future research funding
